'''''Scaevola albida''''', commonly known as '''pale fan-flower'''<ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |last1=Carolin |first1=R.C |title=''Scaevola albida'' |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Scaevola~albida |website=PlantNET-NSW flora online |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |access-date=5 February 2022}}</ref> or '''small-fruit fan-flower''',<ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |title=''Scaevola albida'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/4063a492-eb62-4a10-a418-dc6ee730f824 |website=VICFLORA-flora of Victoria |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Victoria |access-date=5 February 2022}}</ref> is a flowering plant in the family [[Goodeniaceae]], and is [[endemic]] to eastern Australia. It is a prostrate to ascending [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[Herbaceous plant|herb]] with egg-shaped to elliptic leaves, sometimes with toothed edges, pale blue or white fan-shaped flowers and elliptic fruit.

==Description==
''Scaevola albida'' is a prostrate to ascending perennial herb that typically grows up to {{cvt|50|cm}} high with stems sometimes covered with soft hairs. The leaves are elliptic to egg-shaped, wavy, bright green, semi-succulent and slightly hairy, {{cvt|0.6-5|cm}} long, {{cvt|1-25|mm}} wide, margins smooth or toothed, and [[sessile (botany)|sessile]]. The flowers are borne in upper leaf axils on stems up to {{cvt|25|cm}} long, with five white, pale blue or lilac petals, {{cvt|5-10|mm}} long with white, more or less flattened hairs on the outer surface. Flowering occurs mostly from October to January and the fruit is an urn-like shaped, usually one-seeded, papery fruit {{cvt|2-4|mm}} long.<ref name="RBGS"/><ref name="RBGV"/><ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.slsa.sa.gov.au/site/page.cfm| title=The Native Plants of Adelaide| publisher=Department for Environment and Heritage| accessdate=21 March 2011}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
Thi species was first formally described in 1794 by [[James Edward Smith (botanist)|James Edward Smith]] who gave it the name ''Goodenia albida'' in the ''[[Transactions of the Linnean Society of London]]'', from specimens collected by [[John White (surgeon)|John White]] in [[Port Jackson]].<ref name="APNI1">{{cite web |title=''Goodenia albida'' |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/rest/instance/apni/512911 |publisher=Australian Plant Name Index |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref><ref name="Sm.">{{cite journal |last1=Smith |first1=James Edward |title=An account of two new genera of plants from New South Wales, presented to the Linnean Society by Mr. Thomas Hoy and Mr. John Fairbairn |journal=Transactions of  the Linnean Society of London |date=1794 |volume=2 |page=348 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/760133#page/384/mode/1up |access-date=27 January 2026}}</ref> In 1917, [[George Claridge Druce]] transferred the species to ''Scaevola'' as ''S. albida'' in ''The Botanical Exchange Club and Society of the British Isles''.<ref name="APNI">{{cite web |title=''Scaevola albida'' |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/rest/instance/apni/512900 |publisher=Australian Plant Name Index |access-date=6 February 2022}}</ref><ref name="BHL">{{cite journal |last1=Druce |first1=George |title=''Scaevola albida'' |journal=The Botanical Exchange Club and Society of the British Isles |date=1916 |issue=2 |page=644 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/195177#page/716/mode/1up |access-date=6 February 2022}}</ref> The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] (''albida'') means "white".<ref name="Sharr">{{cite book |author=Francis Aubie Sharr |author-link=Francis Aubie Sharr |title=Western Australian Plant Names and their Meanings |date=2019 |publisher=Four Gables Press |location=Kardinya, Western Australia |isbn=9780958034180 |page=130}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Pale fan-flower grows near coastal scrubland, grassy headlands and ranges in New South Wales, Tasmania, South Australia, Victoria and Queensland.<ref name="RBGS"/>
